title: Add check for valid zip contents during import

timeline.body:
<!-- Hey there. Thank you so much for improving NewPipe, and filling out the details. Having roughly the same layout helps everyone considerably :)-->

#### What is it?
- [x] Bugfix (user facing)
- [ ] Feature (user facing)
- [ ] Codebase improvement (dev facing)
- [ ] Meta improvement to the project (dev facing)

#### Description of the changes in your PR
<!-- While bullet points are the norm in this section, feel free to write free-form text instead of a list -->
This PR 
- adds a filter to the import FilePicker, so that only zip files are shown (no more possible to pick a wrong type)
- adds the method `isValidBackupFile` to `ContentsettingsManager` (in short: checks whether the zip has exactly 2 files and whether they're the necessary ones)
- shows a `SnackBar` if the zip is invalid with the action "Show info" which throws `onError` (that the zip file wasn't created by NewPipe)

#### Fixes the following issue(s)
<!-- Also add any other links relevant to your change. -->
- fixes #5055 

#### Due diligence
- [x] I read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

couldn't i just create a zip with 2 empty files with those names and use that to circumvent those checks?
I guess it would then proceed to crash.

Any exceptions during the importing procedure would need to be catched to fix the problem

Maybe you could also check if `entry.getSize() > 0` here, but I am not sure more checks are needed: if the user manually provides an invalid zip which seems legal it is expected for the app to show an error report. Instead, in case something unexpected happened during exporting, resulting in corrupted files, I also think it would be a good idea to show an error report with information, instead of just showing "invalid zip"

reply.body: Checking the export doesn't ensure that the user picks these "previously proved" files, does it? How about a `Snackbar` with an action to show the error? (Similar to the case when comments couldn't be loaded)
Yeah, I'd prefer a `Snackbar` with a custom message based on what caused the error
Okay, I'll update it then soon.

>couldn't i just create a zip with 2 empty files with those names and use that to circumvent those checks?
I guess it would then proceed to crash.

@XiangRongLin Yes, it would crash. But I think that the probability for this case (creating a zip with these filenames by hand) is pretty low - the probability to pick some other zip within the folder is higher (also happened to me once :`) )

>Any exceptions during the importing procedure would need to be catched to fix the problem

In fact, the import procedure is wrapped inside a `try-catch`-block, so every exception should be caught, but unfortunately the app just freezes and restarts without an error screen.
@vkay94 could you rebase and apply the review? Then I think this can be merged.
With the rebase you have to put you logic into `ContentSettingsManager`. Also add a unit test for you scenario, since it's possible here

timeline.body: Why set length to `Snackbar.LENGTH_LONG` just to override it with 3000?

reply.body: I tested it, the SnackBar disappeared pretty fast (subjectively). But I can also remove it.
Can't you just directly write 3000 in the `make` method instead of `Snackbar.LENGTH_LONG`?

The signature of `SnackBar.make` requires the `Duration` interface:
```java
public static Snackbar make(@NonNull View view, @NonNull CharSequence text, @Duration int duration)
```
I just looked into the implementation and the method calls `setDuration`. It should work :)
